item.title: Volt Typhoon exploits Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2024-21762 to maintain access to US critical infrastructure
item.description: The PRC-aligned actor tracked as Volt Typhoon is exploiting an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Fortinet FortiGate appliances (CVE-2024-21762) to compromise edge devices and pivot into operational technology networks. Mandiant observed living-off-the-land lateral movement, credential dumping from LSASS, and the deployment of webshells on the VPN appliance. C2 traffic was observed to 185.225.74.10 and the domain login-portal-update.com. SHA256 of the dropped beacon: 3b8e7d9c2f1a0b6d4e5f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d.

item.title: Scattered Spider runs MFA-fatigue and help-desk social engineering against US insurance firms
item.description: Scattered Spider (aka Octo Tempest, Muddled Libra) is targeting US insurance firms with vishing calls to help desks, MFA push-bombing, and OAuth illicit-consent grants in Entra ID. After initial access the group deploys ScreenConnect and AnyDesk for persistence and exfiltrates data via mega.nz before deploying ransomware. The financial and insurance sector should consider this an active campaign.

item.title: Cl0p ransomware abuses CVE-2025-3104 in MOVEit Transfer for mass data theft
item.description: The Cl0p ransomware crew is again exploiting a zero-day in MOVEit Transfer, this time CVE-2025-3104, to drop a webshell and exfiltrate data from managed file transfer instances at finance and healthcare organisations. Talos reports the use of a custom .NET webshell, archive staging with 7z, and exfiltration to transfer.sh and anonfiles.com. Observed IP: 91.219.236.50.

item.title: BumbleBee loader returns with SocGholish fake-update lures dropping IcedID and Cobalt Strike
item.description: Proofpoint and Unit42 observed renewed BumbleBee activity delivered via SocGholish (FakeUpdates) JavaScript injects on compromised WordPress sites. Post-execution, operators dropped IcedID and Cobalt Strike beacons configured for HTTPS C2. Persistence was established via scheduled tasks and a Run key. SHA256: 9c2f1a0b6d4e5f9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6b5c4d3e2f1a0b9c8d7e6f5a.

item.title: APT29 (Midnight Blizzard) compromises Microsoft 365 tenants via OAuth abuse and password spraying
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has attributed a new wave of Microsoft 365 tenant compromises to APT29 (Midnight Blizzard / Cozy Bear). The Russian SVR-linked group is performing password spraying against legacy authentication endpoints, then granting itself illicit OAuth consent to read mail and files in Entra ID. Government and education sectors are most affected.

item.title: Akira ransomware operators exploit exposed Cisco ASA VPNs without MFA
item.description: CISA and partners warn that Akira ransomware affiliates continue to gain initial access via Cisco ASA SSL VPN portals where MFA is not enforced, often using credentials obtained from RedLine and Lumma Stealer logs. Lateral movement is conducted with RDP and PsExec, followed by data exfiltration via Rclone to mega.nz and encryption of ESXi datastores. Manufacturing and healthcare sectors are heavily targeted. IOC IPs include 45.61.136.215 and 193.143.1.205.

item.title: Beer-and-pretzels review of a vendor whitepaper
item.description: This article discusses the importance of a strong security culture and offers a high-level overview of cybersecurity strategy. No specific CVEs, IOCs, or threat actors are referenced. It is provided as a negative-control item for the scoring engine.
